column8: Mon 16 Nov: store, background to 3f too timid at most: building and pricing the readers' plan resembles a counter-plan debate, but this is a lab result on students with no effect sizes read, and 3f never names the method.

Mon 16 Nov: store only: row 5 (Chanin and Simko) finds the opposite on satisfaction, and the copout is told so its holder would accept it for RANKING_5's reason (the teammate is never the fool), not for this one.
Mon 16 Nov: store: answers with whom for row 1 (fast-advancing middle managers as well as students), still a lab on case problems, abstract only; pairs with row 1 if 3f ever leans on the lab result.

Mon 16 Nov: store and the References check: never cite Schwenk 1990 for debate beating consensus; the fair line is that a planned critic beat a single expert's plan, and the counter-plan's edge vanished on ill-structured tasks like Laura's.
Mon 16 Nov: writers' guard for 3f: two results run the other way, so never say consensus is bad; agreement reached after a test is the goal, agreement in place of a test the risk; small samples.

Mon 16 Nov: store only: the tone of an assigned critic in a lab; the copout was a teammate's own objection, not a role (row 25), so the carping finding serves no moment, and RANKING_5 already sets how the objection is told.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: assigned-critic groups considered more alternatives in the lab, but too timid had no assigned critic and the 1995 comparison groups were not read.
Mon 16 Nov: the older, smaller meta-analysis; row 9's larger one finds no overall relation, so quote the pair through row 9 and never -.23 alone.

Mon 16 Nov: 3f closing, why disagreements are judged by their tests: re-read at source 16 Nov, the paper's headline is rho = -.01 (neither positive nor negative); -.07 (k 92) is its pooled matrix for the path model; say no relation overall, more positive in top management teams (.09) and on decision quality, never slightly worse; fix claim 1's -.07 to -.23 the same way.

Mon 16 Nov: store: a practitioners' summary of the dissent research; its use is a writer guard (no groupthink frame in 3f); if row 13's checklist is used, quote its questions, never its groupthink heading.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: the honest limit on rows 1-3 (lab results may not generalise); Mason is second-hand, so never quoted.

Mon 16 Nov: store, 3f closing at most: process beat analysis six to one in managers' own reports, with a halo risk the authors name; 3f judges three dated moments, and a consultancy survey adds a claim the team cannot test.

Mon 16 Nov: 3f closing paragraph: a reviewer's yardstick in Kahneman, Lovallo and Sibony's words, answered with dates (the objection of 5 Oct; four alternative funds and floors from $150,000 down to $50,000 priced); re-read at source 16 Nov; the same checklist asks 'Is the recommending team overly cautious?' (question 12), the too timid charge, so it covers two moments; quote the questions, never its groupthink heading.

Mon 16 Nov: store, or one clause in 3f's closing if a classic is wanted: Sloan adjourning a unanimous meeting is vivid, but it praises disagreement for existing, which row 9 says proves nothing without a test; Sloan only as Drucker reports him.

Mon 16 Nov: store: groups reason to the answer when a test can settle the argument; the knife edge and the copout had one, but a plan has no provable answer, so background for why each moment ends on a test.
Mon 16 Nov: store, 3f knife edge as framing at most: with no dissenter, the team made a year of closes its other side; a theory paper, so it explains and never proves.

Mon 16 Nov: store only: team-run funds hold less extreme, less concentrated portfolios, an echo of keeping the whole market, but the copout was settled by a bar set first, not by averaging views; never the Patel and Sarkissian performance clause, since fund returns are no evidence for Laura's plan.

Mon 16 Nov: store: corrects Q13-018's number of quality solutions to mainly quantity (quality alone not significant, F(2, 52) = 1.28; combined measure p < .06); if 3f leans on authentic dissent it says more ideas, not better ones; unit counts unsettled.
Mon 16 Nov: twin of Q13-018 (real dissent opens reconsideration, a role-played critic breeds bolstering); a mock-jury design with no discussion adds nothing the copout needs beyond that row.
Mon 16 Nov: store: with 201 working adults, real disagreement beat an assigned critic at stopping one-sided search; backs Q13-018 with a stronger sample, and 3f still never names the method.

Mon 16 Nov: 3f copout, one clause at most: dissent raised solution rates even when no member's first choice was right, through more intense discussion (abstract re-read at source 16 Nov); but those groups found an answer none held, while the team kept its first choice, so say the objection forced the reasons into the open, never that dissent paid because the proposal lost; the 27%, 7% and 62% are from the 2012 review, cite it.

Mon 16 Nov: store only: the study's structure was an assigned-critic procedure, which no moment used (row 25), and an escalation-of-commitment study beside the decision to keep VT invites the reading that the team escalated; never pair it with the copout.

Mon 16 Nov: store only as general background on independent judgements: the record gives neither who the too timid readers were nor whether they judged apart (RANKING_5; blind_key_3 E4), so never argue three verdicts as three independent signals.
Mon 16 Nov: a review restating Q13-018 (genuine over contrived advocacy); its anonymity point concerns the readers, whom the report never describes (RANKING_5), so nothing for 3f.

Mon 16 Nov: 3f writers' guard, checked against BLIND_POOL_3 E1, E3, E4 and RANKING_5: the copout a teammate's own objection, too timid a verdict from readers asked only to rank plans (never who they were), the knife edge no dissenter; so 3f never says devil's advocate, and Q13-018's guard now covers all three moments.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: adds the measured drop in confidence (25.0 points against 14.0 and 12.4) to Q13-002; no moment was a premortem (row 36), so it serves no part.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: premortem teams found more and better risks (abstract; the sample of 101 unverified); no moment was a premortem.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: a premortem works through the group's talk, not the failure frame alone; a master's thesis with small samples, and no moment was a premortem.
Mon 16 Nov: store only: drop its use, which maps a premortem study onto the knife edge; row 36 says the knife edge priced a real failure on 185 closes, not an imagined one.

Mon 16 Nov: 3f copout, its evaluation: criteria fixed before the applicant's gender was known removed the bias, so the 30 Sep bar, five days before the objection, left no room to call 0.8991 against 0.90 a pass (re-read at source 16 Nov); fix the disanalogy before use: the commitment test (Experiment 3) used 117 beach and fair visitors, not undergraduates, and the bias it removed was men's; a closer fit than Q13-019, which it should lead.
Mon 16 Nov: twin of row 30: a news quote and a 2020 replication its authors call suggestive; row 30's backing, never a second citation in 3f.

Mon 16 Nov: 3f knife edge: the team asked for a second doctor on good news; re-read at source 16 Nov (13 of 25 retested, 52%, against 4 of 22, 18%; the quote is in the introduction); fix the base: 173 of 185 closes to 25 Sep, never every close of 2026 beside 173 of 185 (8b's year is 37 of 214 to 6 Nov); the paper's text says 76.5 s where its table says 75.5, so leave the seconds out.

Mon 16 Nov: the same mechanism as row 32 in summary form (Can I believe this? Must I?); Ditto and Lopez is the measured experiment behind it; Kunda's point on reasonable-sounding reasons also backs row 30.

Mon 16 Nov: 3f copout or the writers' brief: the measured cost of choosing outcomes after the results (17 of 30 trials positive before 2000, 2 of 25 after; chi-square 12.2, p = 0.0005; re-read at source 16 Nov); the authors say they cannot claim cause, so say coincided with; one clause at most beside row 30, which fits a choice between candidates more closely.

Mon 16 Nov: 3f too timid and the 27 Nov writers' brief: resolving to be unbiased did not help and a procedure did, so each moment shows its procedure (the readers' plan built and priced), never we stayed open-minded; a 2023 test found it in one study of two, so cite it as a finding, not a law.

Mon 16 Nov: 3f writers' guard, checked against RANKING_5 and BLIND_POOL_3: no moment imagined a failure; the knife edge priced a real one, the copout set a bar first, the first plan's 27 Sep run counted simulated misses; supersedes Q13-001's use (the 27 Sep test as a pre-mortem done with numbers).

Mon 16 Nov: 3f closing: only the copout had a bar written before its result; the knife edge's yardstick was the $300,000 deposit and too timid's verdict met no bar written first, so say each moment ends on what changed or was tested and kept, with one line on luck (RANKING_5's own rule), and keep the bar for the copout.

Mon 16 Nov: the same finding and moment as row 32; carry its luck line (fills within two trading days of the year's cheapest close, timing not skill, 8b) and the completion rule's reason into row 32's use, with 173 of 185 closes to 25 Sep.
Mon 16 Nov: row 35's finding with the moment's facts as RANKING_5 gives them (29 Sep model on a design since revised; today's trade NUMBERS 8n); one row in the store; the readers are never described.
Mon 16 Nov: row 30's bar plus row 21's dissent with E1's dates; the dissent half carries row 21's fix (the team kept its first choice), and Trading Note 3 is never the moral.
